edit.description: the phase override, and the default that survives it

summary: pkgManagerGate pins when: afterCommit, so a chain moving tsc to the merged tree must hand-roll shellGate — placement is spec'd as the chain's

per.section: Gate placement is the chain's decision

tests: tscGate({ when: 'afterMerge' }) returns a gate whose phase is afterMerge
pins: tscGate, vitestGate and eslintGate stay at afterCommit when called with no override
acceptance: `PkgManagerOverride` carries `when`, the three builtins thread it into `shellGate`, and an omitted `when` still yields `afterCommit`.
notes: From DISPATCHER-EXTRACT-FRICTION's afterMerge revert. `pkgManagerGate` (src/builtinGates.ts:151) hardcodes when:'afterCommit', so a chain wanting the same check on the merged tree copies the builtin's own cmd/args into shellGate — engine-boundary.md *Surface, not prescription*, verbatim copying is the detector. Where this chain then puts it is the human's (open question, same tick).

edit.description: the plan ladder's agreement claim drives a real tick

summary: tests/chain.test.ts folds this chain's ladder off a hand-built TickResult, so an engine-side rename of the handoff vocabulary ships green

per.section: A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote

pins: this chain's plan ladder routes the baton from a TickResult the dispatcher produced
acceptance: At least one plan-slice rung transition is read off a real `Dispatcher.tick()` outcome instead of the `tickResult()` fixture; the build-wave legs that remain are the declared debt below.
notes: From CASCADE-LADDER-DRIVEN-BY-A-REAL-TICKRESULT's note; template is tests/examples.test.ts:475. tests/chain.test.ts:231-296 hand-folds pickableAfter/noCommit/entries[] through `tickResult()`. Unlike cascade, the slices declare `agent: planAgent`, so DispatcherOptions.agent never reaches them — swap the agent on the factory's phases, the one override, as setupWorktree already is there. Slice gates are cheap, so the fast lane holds. Build-wave legs out of scope.
